Encrypt a payload as a JWE

Source: R/jwe.R
jwe_encrypt.Rd

jwe_encrypt() encrypts plaintext to one recipient, or to several through jwe_recipient(), and returns the JWE in the compact, flattened JSON or general JSON serialization (RFC 7516).

Usage

jwe_encrypt(
  plaintext,
  key,
  alg = NULL,
  enc = "A128CBC-HS256",
  header = NULL,
  unprotected = NULL,
  aad = NULL,
  format = c("compact", "flattened", "general")
)

Arguments

plaintext

The plaintext: a raw vector, or a single string taken as UTF-8 text.

key

A jwk, or a list of jwe_recipient() objects for several recipients.

alg

The key management algorithm, such as "A256KW", "A256GCMKW", "PBES2-HS256+A128KW" or "dir". NULL takes the key's own alg.

enc

The content encryption algorithm. "A128CBC-HS256" is the one RFC 7518 requires every implementation to support.

header

Further protected header members, as a named list. For PBES2-*, p2c sets the iteration count.

unprotected

Shared unprotected header members, as a named list. Only the JSON serializations carry them.

aad

Additional authenticated data, as a raw vector or a string. Only the JSON serializations carry it.

format

"compact", "flattened" or "general". Several recipients need "general".

Value

The JWE, as a single string.

Details

Every message gets a fresh content encryption key and initialization vector, drawn from the operating system's cryptographic random source through zucrypt. They cannot be supplied: a reused IV or CEK breaks the encryption. If the random source fails, the error is zucrypt's zucrypt_entropy_error, and nothing is returned.

Key management is dir, A128KW, A192KW, A256KW, A128GCMKW, A192GCMKW, A256GCMKW, one of the PBES2-* algorithms, or RSA-OAEP or RSA-OAEP-256 to an RSA public key of at least 2048 bits, or ECDH-ES, ECDH-ES+A128KW, ECDH-ES+A192KW or ECDH-ES+A256KW to an EC key on P-256, P-384 or P-521 or an X25519 key. ECDH-ES generates a fresh ephemeral key, written as epk, and takes apu and apv from header; in direct mode (ECDH-ES) it encrypts to one recipient. RSA1_5 is refused: it is accepted by jwe_decrypt() only, when algorithms names it, and it never encrypts. Content encryption is A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384, A256CBC-HS512, A128GCM, A192GCM or A256GCM. A*GCMKW writes the key wrapping iv and tag into the header, and PBES2-* writes a random 16-byte p2s; none of the three can be given.

For PBES2-* the key is the password, as an oct key: jwk_oct(charToRaw(enc2utf8(password))). The iteration count is p2c in header, a whole number of at least 1000, and defaults to 600 000. A recipient decrypting with jwe_decrypt() accepts at most jose_limits()$p2c iterations, by default also 600 000.

See also

jwe_decrypt().

Examples

key <- jwk_generate("oct", alg = "A128KW", kid = "kek")
token <- jwe_encrypt("secret", key)
token
#> [1] "eyJhbGciOiJBMTI4S1ciLCJlbmMiOiJBMTI4Q0JDLUhTMjU2Iiwia2lkIjoia2VrIn0.PPx6FbuP-ZeLIVpAPa3OgKIOfC-6-pUHkM2jPAuvppa_ahS2-nh3lg.vofWZ4sL0usyVY9ZUS4XSQ.CcgiLyNuvzRAmi8RPNOF1g.txtuRMiQOQ6yH4zIGXQzvw"
jwe_decrypt(token, key, algorithms = "A128KW",
             encryptions = "A128CBC-HS256")
#> <jwe_decrypted> A128KW with A128CBC-HS256, key "kek"
#> Header:
#>   alg: "A128KW"
#>   enc: "A128CBC-HS256"
#>   kid: "kek"
#> Plaintext: 6 bytes

# AES-GCM content encryption, under a password.
password <- jwk_oct(charToRaw("correct horse battery staple"))
token <- jwe_encrypt("secret", password, alg = "PBES2-HS256+A128KW",
                      enc = "A256GCM", header = list(p2c = 10000))
jwe_decrypt(token, password, algorithms = "PBES2-HS256+A128KW",
             encryptions = "A256GCM")$plaintext
#> [1] 73 65 63 72 65 74
